para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“At all times” means 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

“Board-certified” means a physician certified by a member board of the American Board of Medical Specialties, or the equivalent as defined in the Health Occupations Article, § 14-101, Annotated Code of Maryland, and maintaining current board certification.
“Capability” means having the necessary equipment and supplies as well as staff with the skill and experience in its use.
“Continuously available” means a resource that is available at all times, either on-site or on-call.
“Current” means generally accepted, used, practiced, or prevalent at the moment.
“Dedicated” means a resource is assigned to or for the exclusive use by a unit and not shared with any other unit
“E” means the standard is essential.
“Immediately available” means a resource that is available at all times, as soon as it is requested.
“NA” means the standard does not apply.
“O” means the standard is optional.
“On-site” means physically present in the hospital.

“Programmatic responsibility” means the writing, review, and maintenance of practice guidelines, policies, and procedures; development of the operating budget in collaboration with hospital administration and other program directors; evaluation and guiding of the purchase of equipment; planning, development, and coordinating of educational programs, both in-hospital and outreach; participation in the evaluation of perinatal care; and participation in perinatal quality improvement and patient safety activities.

“Readily available” means a resource is available for use a short time after it is requested, and able to be physically present on-site within a timeframe that incorporates maternal and fetal or neonatal risk and benefits with the provision of associated care.

“Telehealth” means the use of interactive technology assisted communications by a licensed health care provider, who is at a different physical location that the patient, to provide health care service within the scope of practice of the health care provider. Telehealth consultation between provider and patient must include audio and video components, must be synchronous with an exchange of information that occurs in real time, and must be in compliance with Health Occupations Article, § 1-1001, Annotated Code of Maryland, and COMAR 10.32.05.

tr.td: A. The hospital’s Board of Directors, administration, and medical and nursing staffs shall demonstrate commitment to its specific level of perinatal center designation and to the care of perinatal patients. This commitment shall be demonstrated by:

(1) A Board of Directors’ commitment that the hospital agrees to meet the current Maryland Perinatal System Standards for its specific level of designation and assures that all perinatal patients shall receive medical care commensurate with that designation;

(2) Submission of patient care data to the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), as requested, for system and quality management; and

(3) A Board of Directors’ resolution, bylaws, contracts, and budgets indicating the hospital’s commitment to the financial, human, and physical resources and to the infrastructure that are necessary to support the hospital’s level of perinatal center designation.
B. The hospital shall be licensed by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) as an acute care hospital.

C. The hospital shall be accredited by an organization that has been granted deeming authority by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and approved by the Maryland Department of Health to accredit hospitals in the State.

D. The hospital shall have an agreement with the Health Services Cost Review Commission that addresses how the cost of neonatal intensive care services will be incorporated into the hospital’s population health budget, and the hospital shall have a certificate of need (CON) from the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) in order to provide neonatal intensive care services, defined as a Level III or IV perinatal program, unless establishment of the hospital’s neonatal intensive care services preceded this requirement. A hospital shall obtain a CON in order to establish Level III or IV perinatal program or to expand a Level III perinatal program to Level IV.

E. The hospital shall obtain and maintain current equipment and technology, as described in these standards, to support optimal perinatal care for the level of the hospital’s perinatal center designation.
F. If maternal or neonatal air transports are accepted, then the hospital shall have a heliport, helipad, or access to a helicopter landing site near the hospital.

G. section.heading: Designated Comprehensive Stroke Center.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.01, a designated comprehensive stroke center hospital shall:

para.text: Be designated by MIEMSS as a primary stroke center or thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center at the time of application for designation as a comprehensive stroke center;
Continue to meet the primary stroke center requirements in COMAR 30.08.11 to the extent such requirements are consistent with designation as a comprehensive stroke center;
Act as a resource center for other facilities in its region or state;
Annually care for at least 20 subarachnoid hemorrhage by aneurysm patients per year;
Annually perform a combined total of 15 endovascular coiling and surgical clippings for aneurysm per year;
Administer fibrinolytics to 25 eligible patients per year or 50 eligible patients over 2 years:
IV fibrinolytic ordered and monitored via telemedicine at another hospital is acceptable; and
IV fibrinolytic administered at an outside hospital and transferred to the comprehensive stroke center site is acceptable;
Satisfy the requirements for designation as a comprehensive stroke center by MIEMSS; and
Meet the requirements for a site review in COMAR 30.08.02.06, which may be satisfied by completing either:
An on-site review by MIEMSS; or
A site survey as part of The Joint Commission Disease Specific Care Certification Program for certification as a comprehensive stroke center if the hospital:

Authorizes The Joint Commission to provide MIEMSS with survey findings, certification reports, and other information related to The Joint Commission's certification of the hospital as a comprehensive stroke center;
Allows MIEMSS to participate in the accreditation and certification site surveys; and
Provides MIEMSS any additional information required to determine it has satisfied the requirements for designation under this chapter.

section.heading: Organization.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.02.

section.heading: Emergency Department.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.03.

section.heading: Neuroscience Intensive Care Unit.
section.text: The hospital shall maintain a dedicated neuroscience intensive care unit that meets the requirements of this regulation that:

para.text: Has designated beds for the care of acute stroke patients;
Has at all times on-site with neurovascular training (e.g., APNs, PAs, Neuro-Intensivists, Fellows, and Residents);
Provides care to acute stroke patients through qualified clinical staff who meet the requirements in Regulations .12—.15 of this chapter;
Follows standardized processes derived from evidence-based practice clinical practice guidelines to facilitate clinical care;
Incorporates individualized plans of care that are based on the patient’s assessed needs and reflect coordination of care with other programs, as determined by patient comorbidities;
Has a process to assess the abilities and resources of family members to be involved in post-acute care; and
Maintains written documentation delineating the function of the neuroscience intensive care unit, including:
Admission criteria;
Discharge criteria;
Acute stroke care protocols;
Interdisciplinary rounding;
Rehabilitation assessment and services in the hospital; and
Outcome data.

section.heading: Stroke Unit.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.07, the hospital shall:

para.text: Have sufficient personnel available to respond to health care personnel at other hospitals to provide them with guidance and recommendations about the diagnosis and treatment of stroke and referral to an appropriate facility if transfer is required or requested;
Have written policies or procedures to direct the organized, safe, intra-hospital and inter-hospital transport of stroke patients;
Have priority bed availability for stroke patients with appropriately trained registered nurses in sufficient numbers based on patient acuity; and

Have a written plan for triaging patients from the neuroscience intensive care unit and/or the dedicated this unit to make beds available for other stroke patients when necessary or for provision of alternate critical care beds for stroke patients with appropriately trained registered nurse staff.

section.heading: Stroke Team.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.05.

section.heading: Operating Room.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.04, the hospital shall have:

para.text: An attending board certified/board eligible neurosurgeon on call with a 30-minute arrival time to the hospital;
Written procedures or protocols demonstrating the ability to meet the emergent needs of multiple complex neurosurgical stroke patients at one time.

section.heading: Endovascular Interventional Services.
section.text: The hospital shall have:

para.text: Interventional services promptly available at all times with appropriately trained support staff and equipment, to perform:
Intra-arterial reperfusion therapy;
Endovascular treatment of vasospasm;
Endovascular ablation of arterial venous malformations;
Stenting/angioplasty of extracranial vessels; and
Stenting/angioplasty of intracranial vessels;
A neurointerventionalist who may be a board-certified/board-eligible neuroradiologist, neurologist, or neurosurgeon on call with a 30-minute arrival time to the hospital;
Written procedures or protocols demonstrating the ability to meet the emergent needs of multiple simultaneous complex stroke patients including assessment and appropriate treatment;
A written protocol to accept the inter-facility transfer of acute ischemic stroke patients requiring endovascular therapy that includes communication and feedback to the sending facility; and
A written protocol to accept the inter-facility transfer of acute stroke patients requiring a higher level of care.

section.heading: Neuroimaging Services.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.09, the hospital shall have the following diagnostic capability available when indicated:

para.text: Carotid duplex ultrasound;
Transcranial ultrasonography; and
Transesophageal or transthorasic echocardiogram.

section.heading: Qualifications of Stroke Center Director and Clinicians.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.10, the hospital’s clinical staff shall meet the following:

para.text: The stroke center medical director’s qualifications shall include:
Completion of a stroke fellowship or vascular neurosurgery fellowship and obtained vascular neurology certification by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology;
Participation in at least one regional, national, or international stroke conference annually;
Participation in stroke patient morbidity and mortality reviews; and
Participation in stroke research and publication efforts.
Qualifications for neurologists, neurosurgeons, neurointerventionalists, neuroradiologists, vascular surgeons and neurointensivists shall include:
Board certification or Board eligibility in their specialty as approved by the American Board of Medical Specialties;
Completion of:
A fellowship; or
Demonstrated experience equivalent to completion of a stroke specialty fellowship appropriate to their area of expertise;
Participation in stroke patient morbidity and mortality reviews; and
Participation in stroke research and publication efforts.
Emergency Physicians. The qualifications of emergency physicians who care for stroke patients shall include:
Board certification or Board eligibility in emergency medicine as approved by the American Board of Medical Specialties; and
Participation in stroke patient morbidity and mortality reviews.
Nurse Practitioners who care for stroke patients shall:
Hold a current license with the Maryland State Board of Nursing to practice as a registered nurse;
Maintain certification as a nurse practitioner from the American Nurses Credentialing Center or other certification organization as deemed appropriate by the Maryland State Board of Nursing; and
Be credentialed through the hospital’s credentialing process.
Physician assistants who care for stroke patients shall:
Have graduated from a physician assistant educational program accredited by the Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant or its successor;
Maintain current certification by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants; and
Be credentialed through the hospital credentialing process.

section.heading: Qualifications of Nurses, Nurse Practitioners, and Physician Assistants in the Neuroscience Intensive Care Unit.
section.text: Clinical nurses, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants providing care to stroke patients in the neuroscience intensive care unit shall be trained in assessment of neurological function and management and treatment of all aspects of neurocritical care, including:

para.text: Function of ventriculostomy and external ventricular drainage apparatus;
Monitoring and treatment of increased intracranial pressure;
Care of patients with intracranial hemorrhage and subarachnoid hemorrhage;
Care of patients post fibrinolytic therapy;
Care of patients post mechanical thrombectomy;
Treatment of blood pressure abnormalities using parenteral vasoactive agents;
Management of intubated/ventilated patients; and
Detailed neurological assessments and scales.

section.heading: Qualifications of Nurses, Nurse Practitioners, and Physician Assistants in the Emergency Department.
section.text: Emergency department nurses, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who triage patients in the emergency department or care for acute stroke patients shall be trained in:

para.text: Assessment of acute stroke;
Treatment of acute stroke;
Use of clinically appropriate fibrinolytic in acute ischemic stroke and the indication for endovascular therapy in acute ischemic stroke;
Educated on mechanical thrombectomy protocols;
Treatment of blood pressure abnormalities with parenteral vasoactive agents;
Neurological assessments and scales (i.e., National Institute of Health Stroke Scale and the Glasgow Coma Scale);
Management of intubated/ventilated patients; and
Care of patients post fibrinolytic therapy.

section.heading: Continuing Medical Education Requirements for Nurses, Nurse Practitioners, and Physician Assistants in the Stroke Unit.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.05.

section.heading: Prevention/Public Education.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.12.

section.heading: Policies, Protocols, Guidelines, and Agreements.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.13, the hospital shall:

para.text: Have written policies that demonstrate that the hospital has established the comprehensive stroke center to:
Ensure the transfer of patients from another facility is appropriate and patients are received in a timely manner; and
Ensure that all stroke patients receive care commensurate with the hospital’s designation as a comprehensive stroke center;

Have written care protocols for advanced treatment of complex stroke patients, including, but not limited to, acute ischemic stroke patients, acute intra-arterial therapeutic interventions, management of intracranial hemorrhage, and management of subarachnoid hemorrhage;
Have written procedures demonstrating the ability of neurosurgery and interventional radiology to simultaneously care for two complex stroke patients with appropriate clinicians;
Maintain up-to-date written care protocols for the treatment of acute stroke in:
The neuroscience intensive care unit;
The stroke unit;
The emergency department; and
All other locations where stroke care is provided;
Establish mechanisms to serve and act as a resource center for other facilities in their region or state that shall include:
Providing consultative expertise in managing particular cases;
Offering guidance for triage of patients;
Providing advanced diagnostic, surgical or interventional procedures and treatment to patients initially treated at a non-primary stroke center or a primary stroke center; and
Acting as an educational resource for other hospitals and health care professionals; and

Have written policies and or protocols delineating the scope of practice and the roles and responsibilities of nurse practitioners and physician assistants providing care to the acute stroke patient in the neuroscience intensive care unit, the emergency department, and the stroke unit.
In addition to the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.14, the hospital shall incorporate into the hospital’s quality assurance process reports:
Specific acute stroke treatment benchmarks; and
Stroke treatment quality improvement goals.
The hospital shall establish a multidisciplinary institutional quality assurance/performance improvement committee that meets on a regular basis to:
Monitor quality benchmarks;
Review complications; and
Review and modify practice patterns as appropriate.

In cases where mechanical endovascular reperfusion therapy is appropriate, the hospital shall achieve door-to-device times (arrival to first pass of thrombectomy device) in 50 percent or more of eligible acute ischemic stroke patients within 90 minutes for direct arriving patients and within 60 minutes for inter-facility transfer patients.
The hospital shall demonstrate progress towards reducing door-to-device times to within 90 minutes for 75 percent or more of eligible direct-arriving acute ischemic stroke patients.

section.heading: Designated Acute Stroke Ready Center.
section.text: A designated acute stroke ready center shall:

para.text: Be licensed as a hospital or freestanding medical center by the licensing authority in the jurisdiction in which it is located;

If a hospital, be accredited by an organization that has been granted deeming authority by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and approved by the Maryland Department of Health to accredit hospitals in the State;
If located in Maryland, be a base station approved under COMAR 30.03.06;

Provide assessment and management of the stroke patient consistent with the most current American Heart Association/American Stroke Association consensus based clinical practice guidelines to meet the needs of the patient;
Have a stroke center medical director;
Have a 0.5 (or greater) full-time equivalent (FTE) dedicated stroke center nurse coordinator;
Have sufficient personnel and resources needed to facilitate healthcare data management and concurrent review of quality metrics and program objectives;
Meet the requirements of Regulations .02—.14 of this chapter; and
Meet the requirements for a site review in COMAR 30.08.02.06, which may be satisfied by completing either:
An on-site review by MIEMSS; or
A site survey as part of The Joint Commission Disease Specific Care Certification Program for certification as an acute stroke ready center if the facility:

Authorizes The Joint Commission to provide MIEMSS with survey findings, certification reports, and other information related to The Joint Commission’s certification of the hospital as an acute stroke ready center;
Allows MIEMSS to participate in the accreditation and certification site surveys; and
Provides MIEMSS any additional information required to determine it has satisfied the requirements for designation under this chapter.

section.heading: Organization.
section.text: The facility’s board of directors, administrators, and medical and nursing staff shall demonstrate commitment to the facility’s designation as an acute stroke ready center by:

para.text: A board of directors’ resolution stating that the facility’s commitment to serving as an acute stroke ready center;
An organizational chart showing key stroke center personnel, including the stroke center medical director and the stroke center nurse coordinator and their relationship with the facility;
Establishing mechanisms to guide and assure cooperative relationships with community and professional groups committed to increasing public awareness and improving acute stroke care;
Maintaining documentation of stroke center leadership, including:
An appointment letter for the stroke center medical director; and
Curricula vitae of core team personnel with training and expertise in cerebrovascular disease, including:
Physicians;
Stroke center nurse coordinator; and
Other key health care personnel; and

Maintaining bylaws, contracts, and budgets specific to acute stroke care, indicating the facility’s commitment to the financial, human, and physical resources necessary to support its designation as an acute stroke ready center.

section.heading: Emergency Department.
section.text: The facility shall maintain an emergency department that:

para.text: Has written documentation on the process used to notify the stroke team of a patient with an acute stroke; and
Has sufficient emergency department clinical staff to meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.05.
The facility shall have a written agreement with a hospital that:
Has operating room neurosurgical services available at all times with appropriately trained support staff;
Has neurosurgical coverage documented in a written plan approved by the covering neurosurgeon(s), stroke program leaders, and any involved facilities; and
Has neurosurgical services available to patients within 2 hours of it being deemed necessary.
There shall be a written protocol for transfer that includes communication and feedback from the receiving facility.

The facility shall establish one or more acute stroke teams that shall respond to the emergency department with coordinated services for the effective delivery of emergency and acute stroke treatment.
The facility shall have the following present at the patient’s bedside:
A member of the emergency department clinical staff shall evaluate each patient with stroke-like symptoms within 10 minutes of the patient’s arrival at the emergency department; and
At least one member of the acute stroke team, who may be present via teleneurology, to provide care and to treat an acute stroke patient within 15 minutes of notification.

The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) shall be used for the initial assessment of patients with acute stroke. Clinicians performing the NIHSS will have documented training regarding the completion of the NIHSS.
Patients suspected of having an acute stroke shall undergo continuous monitoring and receive frequent documented neurological assessments.
The acute stroke team shall include at a minimum:
A physician with special competence in caring for the acute stroke patient who is Board certified or Board eligible in:
Neurology;
Emergency medicine;
Family medicine; or
Internal medicine; and
At least one additional health care clinician with experience in caring for the acute stroke patient who may be:
A family medicine physician;
An internist;
An emergency physician;
A registered nurse;
A physician assistant; or
A nurse practitioner.

If the physician who satisfies §C(1) of this regulation is not Board certified or Board eligible in neurology, a Board certified or Board eligible neurologist shall be available within 15 minutes for consultation under the terms of a written agreement by:
Telephone; or
Audio/visual communication.

section.heading: Stroke Unit.
section.text: The facility shall:

para.text: If an acute care hospital, maintain a stroke unit that:
Has designated beds for the care of patients not eligible for fibrinolytic therapy or endovascular therapy with qualified clinical staff who meet the requirements in Regulation .09 of this chapter;
Employs standardized process supported by clinical practice guidelines or evidence-based practice to deliver or facilitate the delivery of clinical care;
Develops an individualized plan of care that is based on the patient’s assessed needs and reflects coordination of care with other programs, as determined by patient comorbidities; and
Maintains written documentation delineating the function of the stroke unit including:
Admission criteria;
Discharge criteria;
Stroke care protocols;
Patient census;
Rehabilitation in the hospital;
Rehabilitation after discharge; and
Outcomes data; or
If not an acute care hospital, have a written transfer agreement with a hospital that:
Meets the requirements of this chapter;
Has an inpatient stroke unit that meets the requirements of this regulation; and
Can admit the patient after initial treatment and stabilization.

section.heading: Laboratory/Diagnostic Services.
section.text: The facility shall have the ability at all times to perform laboratory and diagnostic services within 45 minutes of written order, including but not limited to:

para.text: Complete blood count;
Blood chemistries;
Coagulation studies;
Troponin;
Electrocardiograms; and
Chest radiographs.

section.heading: Neuroimaging Services.
section.text: The facility shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.09.

section.heading: Qualifications of Stroke Center Director and Clinicians.

para.text: The stroke center medical director shall be a physician with special competence in caring for acute stroke patients who is clinically active at the facility and is Board certified or Board eligible in:
Neurology;
Internal medicine; or
Emergency medicine.
The stroke center medical director’s qualifications shall include active engagement in the Stroke Quality Improvement Council (QIC).
The stroke center coordinator’s qualifications shall include active engagement in the stroke QIC.
The stroke center shall provide the following training to non-physician staff:

Initial orientation, education, and training that is pertinent to the program-specific stroke policies and procedures and individual licensed practitioner’s roles and responsibilities on the stroke team;

Ongoing education and training activities that are pertinent to the licensed practitioner’s roles and responsibilities when staff responsibilities change; new or revised policies, procedures, or guidelines are implemented; or other critical changes as defined by the stroke center; and

Training for all staff in the hospital who interact with stroke patients on the recognition of clinical signs and symptoms that require timely notification according to hospital-specific policy and protocol.

section.heading: Qualifications of Emergency Department Clinical Staff.

para.text: Emergency department clinical staff shall participate in cerebrovascular disease educational activities at least two times a year if they:
Triage patients in the emergency department; or
Care for acute stroke patients.
Emergency department clinical staff who triage patients in the emergency department or care for acute stroke patients shall be trained in:
The diagnosis of acute stroke;
Treatment of acute stroke; and
Use of clinically appropriate fibrinolytics and educated on the indication and referral for endovascular therapy in acute ischemic stroke.
Surviving stroke patients and their families shall receive instruction on:
Signs and symptoms of acute stroke, including the importance of activating EMS;
Effects and prognosis of acute stroke;
Potential complications of acute stroke;
Needs and rationales for treatment;
Patient compliance instructions for risk reduction of individual risk factors and secondary prevention programs; and
Post-stroke support services.
The facility shall support and/or participate in acute stroke educational activities developed for EMS personnel which are conducted at least once a year.

section.heading: Policies, Protocols, Guidelines, and Agreements.
section.text: The facility shall develop and implement:

para.text: A written policy which demonstrates that the facility has established the acute stroke ready center to:
Monitor the care delivered to acute stroke patients;
Improve the quality of care delivered to acute stroke patients;
Move patients through the initial acute care phase of their hospital stay in a timely fashion; and
Ensure that all stroke patients will receive medical care commensurate with the hospital designation as an acute stroke ready center;
Written procedures for rapidly activating the stroke team to care for potentially eligible fibrinolytic and endovascular candidates within 15 minutes of notification;
Written care protocols for the treatment of acute stroke which address:
Evaluation of each patient by a member of the emergency department clinical staff within 10 minutes of the patient’s arrival at the hospital emergency department;
At least one member of the stroke team arriving at the acute stroke patient’s bedside within 15 minutes of notification;
Ischemic stroke;
Hemorrhagic stroke;
Stabilization of vital functions;
Initial diagnostic tests;
The use of medications including fibrinolytics;
Care of the potential endovascular candidate; and
Timely and safe patient transfer within 2 hours or less of emergency department arrival or when medically stable;
A current agreement with a transport service to meet the timeline in §C(9) of this regulation; and
A written protocol for transfer that includes communication and feedback from the receiving facility that is:
Updated at least annually; and
Maintained up-to-date in:
The emergency department; and
All other locations where stroke care is provided.

section.heading: Quality Management.
section.text: The facility shall:

para.text: Participate, in a manner approved by the EMS Board, in a stroke registry that includes the data elements tracked by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and the American Heart/American Stroke Get With the Guidelines®-Stroke Registry and enter the required data in the stroke registry within 45 days of the end of each quarter;
Have participated in the stroke registry and maintained a stroke log for a minimum of 6 months prior to time of requesting an application;
Demonstrate ongoing participation in the stroke registry;
Authorize the stroke registry to provide the hospital data to MIEMSS for health oversight activities in a manner approved by the EMS Board;
Establish at least two outcome objectives that:
Are time-specific;
Are measurable;
Reflect tracking and trending of performance measures and indicators; and
Are reviewed in annual comparison studies;
Maintain a stroke log which includes at a minimum the following information for each entry:
The number of times the stroke team was activated;
The stroke team’s response time to the acute stroke patient;
The on-call neurologist’s response time for consultation to the acute stroke patient;
The type or types of diagnostic tests and acute treatment utilized;
The patient’s diagnosis;
Door to IV fibrinolytic time;
Patient complications;
Arrival and departure/transfer times; and
Disposition of the patient;
Monitor its IV fibrinolytic complications, which includes symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage and serious life-threatening systemic bleeding;

Establish at least one stroke center quality assurance medical review committee which shall be a medical review committee under Health Occupations Article, §1-401, Annotated Code of Maryland, as a committee established in the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems which, at least three times a year:
Meets;
Reviews practice patterns; and
Modifies practice patterns as appropriate;
In cases where the administration of fibrinolytics is appropriate:
Administer the fibrinolytic within 60 minutes from the time the patient arrives at the emergency department for greater than or equal to 50 percent of eligible patients; and
Demonstrate progress towards administering fibrinolytics within 60 minutes from the time the patient arrives at the emergency department for greater than or equal to 75 percent of eligible patents;
Demonstrate progress towards reducing time of administration of fibrinolytics to 45 minutes for greater than or equal to 50 percent of eligible patients;
Incorporate into their quality assurance process progress reports about:
Specific acute stroke treatment benchmarks;
Outcomes data on patients transferred for a higher level of care; and
Stroke treatment quality improvement goals; and
Provide MIEMSS with documentation of quality management of the stroke program for review, including, if appropriate:
Problem identification;
Problem analysis;
An action plan;
Implementation of the plan; and
Re-evaluation of the plan.

section.heading: Designated Thrombectomy-Capable Primary Stroke Center.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11, a designated thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center hospital shall:

para.text: Be designated by MIEMSS as a primary stroke center at the time of application for designation as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;
Continue to meet the primary stroke center requirements in COMAR 30.08.11 to the extent such requirements are consistent with designation as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;

Require each physician who performs mechanical thrombectomy to have performed 15 mechanical thrombectomies over the past 12 months or 30 over the past 24 months. The total volume of cases may include procedures performed at other facilities;
Have performed mechanical thrombectomy and have provided post-procedure care for a minimum of 15 patients in the past 12 months or at least 30 patients over the past 24 months;
Meet the requirements of Regulations .01—.15 of this chapter; and
Meet the requirements for a site review in COMAR 30.08.02.06, which may be satisfied by completing either:
An on-site review by MIEMSS; or
A site survey as part of The Joint Commission Disease Specific Care Certification Program for certification as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center if the hospital:

Authorizes The Joint Commission to provide MIEMSS with survey findings, certification reports, and other information related to The Joint Commission’s certification of the hospital as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;
Allows MIEMSS to participate in the accreditation and certification site; and
Provides MIEMSS any additional information required to determine that the hospital has satisfied the requirements for designation under this chapter.

section.heading: Organization.
section.text: The hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.02.

section.heading: Emergency Department.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.03.

section.heading: Operating Room.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.04.

section.heading: Stroke Team.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.05.

section.heading: Intensive Care Unit.
section.text: The hospital shall maintain an intensive care unit that:

para.text: Has designated beds for the care of the acute stroke patient;
Has at all times on-site practitioners with critical care privileges (e.g., Attending Physicians, APNs, PAs, Fellows, or Residents);
Provides care to acute stroke patients by qualified clinical staff who meet the requirements in Regulation .11 of this chapter;
Follows standardized processes derived from evidence-based clinical practice guidelines to facilitate clinical care;
Incorporates individualized plans of care that are based on the patient’s assessed needs and that reflect coordination of care with other programs, as determined by patient comorbidities;
Has a process to assess the abilities and resources of family members to be involved in post-acute care; and
Maintains written documentation delineating the function of the intensive care unit, including:
Admission criteria;
Discharge criteria;
Acute stroke care protocols;
Interdisciplinary rounding;
Rehabilitation assessment and services in the hospital; and
Outcome data.

section.heading: Stroke Unit.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.07.

section.heading: Laboratory/Diagnostic Services.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.08.

section.heading: Neuroimaging Services.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.09, the hospital shall have the following diagnostic capability available when indicated:

para.text: Carotid duplex ultrasound;
Transcranial ultrasonography; and
Transesophageal/transthoracic echocardiogram.

section.heading: Endovascular Interventional Services.
section.text: A hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall have:

para.text: Interventional services promptly available at all times with appropriately trained support staff and necessary equipment;
Interventional services that include:
Intra-arterial reperfusion therapy; and
Stenting/angioplasty of intracranial vessels;

A neurointerventionalist who may be a Board-certified/Board-eligible neuroradiologist, neurologist, or neurosurgeon with hospital credential privileges on-call with a 30-minute arrival time to the hospital; and
Written procedures or protocols demonstrating the ability to simultaneously meet the emergency needs of multiple complex stroke patients, including assessment and appropriate treatment.

section.heading: Qualifications of Stroke Center Director and Clinicians.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.10, qualifications for a neurointerventionalist include performance of 15 mechanical thrombectomies over the past 12 months or 30 over the past 24 months:

section.heading: Qualifications of Emergency Department Clinical Staff.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.11.

section.heading: Prevention/Public Education.
section.text: The hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.12.

section.heading: Policies, Protocols, Guidelines, and Agreements.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.13, a hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall:

para.text: Have written policies ensuring that:
Transfer of patients from another facility is appropriate and patients are received in a timely manner; and
All stroke patients will receive medical care commensurate with the hospital’s designation as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;
Have written procedures demonstrating the ability to care for simultaneous complex interventional radiology stroke patients using appropriate clinical staff;
Have written care protocols for advanced treatment of complex stroke patients, including, but not limited to, acute ischemic stroke patients and acute intra-arterial therapeutic interventions; and

Document and review the scope of practice and the roles and responsibilities of nurse practitioners and physician assistants providing care to the acute stroke patient in the intensive care unit, the emergency department, and the stroke unit.

section.heading: Quality Management.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.14, a hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall:

para.text: Monitor and demonstrate 24-hour post-procedure stroke and death rates of less than or equal to 1 percent for diagnostic neuro-angiography;
Monitor documentation of the reasons potentially eligible ischemic stroke patients did not receive mechanical thrombectomy;

In cases where mechanical endovascular reperfusion therapy is appropriate, achieve door-to-device times, arrival to first pass of thrombectomy device, in 50 percent or more of eligible acute ischemic stroke patients within 90 minutes for direct arriving patients and within 60 minutes for inter-facility transfer patients treated with endovascular therapy; and
Demonstrate progress towards reducing arrival to first pass of thrombectomy device to within 90 minutes for 75 percent or more of eligible acute ischemic stroke patients who arrive directly.

container.heading: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund

para.text: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund is a special, non-lapsing fund established under Public Safety Article, §3-206.1, Annotated Code of Maryland, for the purpose of providing funding to support activities and training by the Commission.
This chapter establishes the procedures and authorizations for the use of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Commission” means the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.
“Department” means the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
“Executive Director” means the Executive Director of the Police and Correctional Training Commissions, or a designee.
“Fund” means the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund.
“Staff” means employees of the Police and Correctional Training Commissions.
The Fund shall receive an annual appropriation pursuant to Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, §7-301, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Fund is not subject to State Finance and Procurement Article, §7-302, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Interest earnings shall be credited to the Fund.
The State Treasurer shall hold the Fund separately, and the State Comptroller shall account for the Fund.
The Fund may only be used to provide funding to the Commission.

section.heading: Use and Administration of the Fund.

para.text: The Fund shall only be used in support of the Commission’s general powers and duties under Public Safety Article, §§3-206.1, 3-207, and 3-208, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Commission, in coordination with the Executive Director, shall:
Establish goals, objectives, and an annual spending plan that supports the duties and responsibilities of the Commission and training needs for law enforcement;
Review and approve proposed expenditures; and
Ensure that each approved expenditure is consistent with Public Safety Article, §3-207, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Executive Director is responsible for fiscal oversight of the Fund.
Staff shall assist the Executive Director with the development of an annual spending plan that is consistent with the Commission’s strategic plan and specific training goals.
The Department will provide administrative staff support to process procurement and fiscal transactions related to the Commission’s approved fund expenditures.
The Executive Director shall provide quarterly updates to the Commission on fund expenditures and initiatives.
Money expended from the Fund is not intended to take the place of funding that would otherwise be appropriated to the Department or Police and Correctional Training Commissions.

para.text: An applicant shall submit:
A completed application to the Board on the form that the Board requires;
To a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8–303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC as required by §A(2) of this regulation by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) this regulation is incomplete or insufficient.
If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to:
Complete the application; and
Provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board in §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application:
Shall be considered abandoned; and
May be destroyed.
Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking licensure shall:
Submit a new application;
Meet all of the requirements for licensure; and
Pay the required fees that are in effect at the time of re-application.
The Board shall place the license of any registered nurse or licensed practical nurse on inactive status if the licensee:

Has not satisfactorily completed 1,000 hours of active nursing practice or graduated from an approved nursing program within the 5-year period immediately preceding the date of anticipated renewal or chooses inactive status;
Completes the biennial application for inactive status; and
Pays all fees.

A licensee on inactive status may not practice nursing in this State. However, a registered nurse on inactive status may use the title “registered nurse”, and a practical nurse on inactive status may use the title “licensed practical nurse”.
A licensee on inactive status may apply for an active status license provided that the licensee:
Meets the renewal requirements of Health Occupations Article, §8-312, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Submits to the Board:
The required application; and
Written, verified evidence that the licensee has submitted to a criminal history records check in accordance with Regulation .13 of this chapter by:
Submitting one complete set of fingerprints required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
Paying all fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.
An additional fee may not be charged to change from inactive to active status.

para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Board” means the Board of Nursing.

“Board-approved course” means an educational offering specific to the case management of the injured worker under the Workers' Compensation Commission which meets the criteria established by the Board.
“Central Repository” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.27.01.01.
“Commission” means the Workers' Compensation Commission.
“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.27.01.01.
Medical Case Management.

“Medical case management” means any type of contact, including electronic, written, and personal, with the injured worker, for the purpose of the planning and coordination of health services appropriate to achievement of medical rehabilitation of the injured worker.
“Medical case management” includes but is not limited to:
Case assessment;
Implementation and coordination of services with the injured worker, family, and health care providers;
Evaluation of treatment results;
Coordinating community re-entry;
Return to work with the employer of injury; and
Referral for further vocational rehabilitation services.
“Medical claims consultant” means a registered nurse who consults on medical aspects of an injured worker's rehabilitation without any contact with the injured worker.
“Multistate licensure privilege” has the meaning set forth in COMAR 10.27.01.01B.
“Registered nurse (RN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice registered nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing.
“RN-WCCM” means a registered nurse-workers' compensation medical case manager.
For certification as an RN-WCCM, an applicant shall:
Hold a current license to practice registered nursing in this State or a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing;
Submit documentation of successful completion of a Board-approved course;
Submit to the Board a completed application for certification as an RN-WCCM;
Pay all fees; and
Submit to a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Board shall include on the RN's license the designation WCCM.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant from out-of-State shall meet the requirements as stated in this regulation.
Unless renewed biennially, a certification to practice as an RN-WCCM expires at the same time as the registered nurse license.
Before certification as an RN-WCCM expires, the RN-WCCM may renew the certification for an additional term, if the RN—WCCM:
Is otherwise entitled to be certified;
Has practiced a minimum of 2,000 hours in the past 2 years as an RN—WCCM;
Submits a completed application for renewal on the form the Board requires;
Pays all fees; and
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §E of this regulation, submits written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.

If the registered nurse does not meet the practice requirement stated in §B(2) of this regulation, the registered nurse shall complete a Board-approved course to be eligible for renewal of the RN-WCCM certification.
Upon notification by the Board that a CHRC is required before the certification can be renewed, a renewal applicant shall comply with all of the requirements under §B of this regulation.
Criminal history records checks for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the certification holder’s birth month as follows:
In 2026 — all applicants with a September or October birth month;
In 2027 — all applicants with an October or November birth month;
In 2028 — all applicants with a November or December birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a December or January birth month;
In 2030 — all applicants with a January or February birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a February or March birth month;
In 2032 — all applicants with a March or April birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with an April or May birth month;
In 2034 — all applicants with a May or June birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a June or July birth month.
In 2036 — all applicants with a July or August birth month; and
In 2037— all applicants with an August or September birth month.

For renewal applicants who are required to submit a CHRC, the Board may not renew a certification without written documentation that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: Exceptions.
section.text: This chapter does not apply to an individual who:

para.text: Other than a certified nursing assistant, practices a health occupation, that the individual is authorized to practice under the Health Occupations Article, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Provides for the gratuitous care of friends, domestic partners, or family members;
Performs nursing assistant tasks while a nursing student enrolled in an accredited nursing program if the individual either:
Is practicing under the direct supervision of qualified faculty or preceptors; or

Successfully completed the portion of the approved nursing education program that the Board determines meets the requirements of an approved nursing assistant training program as described in Regulation .05D of this chapter;
Performs nursing assistant tasks:
While a student enrolled in an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program; and
While practicing under the direct supervision of qualified faculty or preceptors;
Practices as a certified nursing assistant-I for less than 4 months in accordance with 42 CFR §483.35(d);
Performs nursing tasks delegated by a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse so long as the delegated nursing tasks do not become a routine part of the individual's job duties;
Performs nursing tasks delegated by an advanced practice registered nurse in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-02(d), Annotated Code of Maryland; or
Performs technical tasks delegated by a licensed certified midwife in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-02(e), Annotated Code of Maryland.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Acute care nursing assistant training program” means a course of training that meets the acute care nursing assistant training program curriculum approved by the Board.
“Board” means the Maryland Board of Nursing.
“Central Repository” means the Maryland Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
“Certificate” means a certificate issued by the Board to practice as a certified nursing assistant in the State.
Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA).
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” means an individual, regardless of title, who, for compensation and subject to regulations adopted by the Board, routinely performs:
Nursing tasks delegated by a registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or advanced practice registered nurse; or
Technical tasks delegated by a licensed certified midwife.
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” does not include dialysis technician or medication technician.
Certified Nursing Assistant-I (CNA-I).
“Certified nursing assistant-I (CNA-I)” means a CNA who:
Meets the requirements set by the Board and federal law; and
May practice in any practice setting.
“Certified nursing assistant-I (CNA-I)” includes a:
CNA who was certified as a geriatric nursing assistant on March 31, 2026;
Certified medicine aide; and
CNA who is certified under Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-05(c)(5), Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Certified nursing assistant-II (CNA-II)” means a CNA who:
On March 31, 2026, was certified as a CNA but not certified as a geriatric nursing assistant; and
May not practice in a nursing facility or skilled nursing facility.

“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” means the performance of both a State criminal history records check by the Central Repository and a national criminal history records check performed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

“Criminal history record information” means information provided by the criminal history records check regarding an applicant’s criminal arrests, charges, and convictions and other dispositions of criminal charges.
“Good standing” means without an encumbrance that limits or restricts practice, such as revocation, suspension, or probation.
“Nursing assistant competency evaluation” means an examination approved by the Board that:
Determines the competency of the individual to practice as a CNA-I; and
Meets the requirements under federal law.
“Nursing assistant training program” means a course of training approved by the Board that meets the requirements under federal and State law.
“Service member” has the meaning stated in State Government Article, §9-901, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Temporary nurse aide” means an individual who practiced as a geriatric nursing assistant without certification during the national Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Public Health Emergency, as declared on January 31, 2020, and periodically continued by the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services, pursuant to the waiver of the requirements of 42 CFR §483.35(d) issued by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services on March 6, 2020.
“Technical task” means a routine clinical act or task that does not require clinical judgment and is performed with the supervision as specified in COMAR 10.69.02.
“Temporary nurse aide training” means an 8-hour online training and examination program offered by:
The American Health Care Association;
The National Center for Assisted Living; or
Another comparable program approved by the Board.
Fees are as follows:
Initial certification fee — $20;
Endorsement fee — $20;
Renewal fee — $40;
Verification of certification to another jurisdiction — $25;
Returned check fee — $25;
Duplicate certificate fee — $10.
Fees are not refundable.
An applicant shall submit:
A completed application to the Board on the form that the Board requires;
To a CHRC in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC as required by §A(2) of this regulation by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under §A(2) of this regulation;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) of this regulation is incomplete or insufficient.

If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to complete the application and provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board under §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application shall be considered abandoned and may be destroyed.

Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking CNA certification shall submit a new application on the form required by the Board and meet all of the requirements for CNA certification and pay the required fees that are in effect at the time of re-application.
Initial Certification. An applicant for initial nursing assistant certification shall have successfully:
Completed:
An approved nursing assistant training program;
An approved acute care nursing assistant training program;
A portion of an approved nursing education program that has been determined by the Board to meet the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board; or

Service member training and education that has been determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent to a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §1-702, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Passed a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant for nursing assistant certification by endorsement shall:
Hold a certificate to practice as a nursing assistant that:

Was issued by another state or territory of the United States that has certification requirements that are essentially similar to those set forth in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-05, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Is in good standing; and
Have successfully completed a nursing assistant training program that meets the standards for an approved nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
Any applicant for nursing assistant certification may not have:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification under Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-10, Annotated Code of Maryland; or

A record of abuse, negligence, or misappropriation of a client's property or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any other state or territory of the United States against the certification of the CNA.
Nursing Education Programs.
To meet the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board, a portion of a nursing education program must include courses with content that primarily focuses on:
Nursing fundamentals;
Mental health;
Health assessment;
Nursing ethics; and
The content listed under 42 CFR §483.152(b).

If a portion of a nursing education program does not include courses with content that primarily focuses on the subject matters set forth in § D(1) of this regulation, the Board may review and approve other equivalent subject matters as meeting the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
A CNA-II who seeks certification as a CNA-1 shall meet the qualifications set forth in §A of this regulation.
Temporary Nurse Aides.
A temporary nurse aide applying for certification as a CNA-1 shall be deemed to have completed a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board if the temporary nurse aide:
Completed a temporary nurse aide training course;
Completed a minimum of 100 hours of on-the-job training as a temporary nurse aide that:
Met the requirements under 42 CFR §483.152(a) and 42 CFR §483.152(b)(2)—(7); and
Was not provided in a facility described under 42 CFR §483.151(b)(2)—(3); and
In addition to the minimum 100 hours of on-the-job training, worked as a temporary nurse aide competently for a minimum of 160 hours.

A temporary nurse aide whose on-the-job training did not meet all of the requirements under 42 CFR 483.152(a) and 42 CFR 483.152(b)(2)—(7) may receive supplemental training in those requirements and be deemed to meet the requirement of §F(1)(b)(i) of this regulation.
Initial Certification.
An applicant for initial certification shall:
Comply with all of the requirements under Regulation .04A of this chapter;
Pay the required fee to the Board; and
Submit to the Board one of the items in §A(2) of this regulation.
Verification Requirements.

For graduates of a nursing assistant or acute care nursing assistant training program, an application that has been signed by the program coordinator or faculty of the training program completed by the applicant;

For service members, documentation demonstrating successful completion of service member training and education that has been determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent to a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board;

For nursing students and graduates, an official transcript demonstrating successful completion of a portion of an approved nursing education program that the Board determines meets the requirements for a nursing assistant training program set by the Board; or

For foreign-educated nursing graduates, a copy of an evaluation of the applicant’s transcript through a Board-approved vendor demonstrating successful completion of a portion of an approved nursing education program that meets the requirements for a nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
A program coordinator or faculty of a nursing assistant or acute care nursing assistant training program:
May sign an application before graduation; and
Shall submit written verification, as required by the Board, of program completion to the Board after 5 business days of the applicant’s program completion.

An applicant shall submit an application for initial certification after 24 months of the date of completion of an approved nursing assistant training program, an approved acute care nursing assistant training program, or portion of an approved nursing education program.

If an applicant fails to meet §A(4) of this regulation, an applicant still seeking certification shall take or re-take an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program and comply with §A(4) of this regulation.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant for nursing assistant certification by endorsement shall:
Comply with all of the requirements under Regulation .04A of this chapter;
Pay the required fee to the Board; and
Submit the following verifications directly to the Board from the appropriate authority:
A certificate to practice as a nursing assistant in good standing from another state or territory with certification requirements that are essentially similar to the requirements in this State; and
A certificate of completion from a nursing assistant training program in that state or territory that meets the standards for an approved nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
Every applicant shall attest on the application whether the applicant has:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification; and

A record of abuse, neglect, or misappropriation of a client’s property or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any state or territory of the United States against the certification of the applicant.
A CNA-II who seeks certification as a CNA-I shall:
Submit an application to the Board on the form required by the Board; and
Comply with §§A(1)(c) and A(3)—(5) of this regulation.
A temporary nurse aide applying for certification as a CNA-1 shall:
Comply with §A of this regulation; and
Ensure that the administrator, director of nursing, or human resources representative of the applicant’s employer submits to the Board an attestation, on the form required by the Board, that:
Is completed by the:
Applicant;
Registered Nurse instructor or supervisor of the applicant during employment; and
Administrator or director of nursing for the employer; and
Verifies that the applicant satisfies the requirements of Regulation .05F of this chapter.
An individual is eligible to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation if the individual:
Meets the education requirements set forth in Regulation .05A(1) of this chapter; or
Must retake a nursing assistant competency evaluation in order to renew or reinstate a certification in accordance with Regulation .10C(2)(a) of this chapter.

Except for service members, an individual shall sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation after 24 months of meeting the educational requirements set forth in Regulation .05A(1) of this chapter.

An individual who fails to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation after 24 months of meeting the educational qualifications must re-take an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program in order to be eligible to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
Re-testing.
An individual who fails to obtain a passing score on the first examination may retake a nursing assistant competency evaluation three additional times.
An individual shall wait at least 45 calendar days from the date of the prior evaluation before retaking a nursing assistant competency evaluation.

An individual who fails to obtain a passing score after taking a nursing assistant competency evaluation four times must complete a new approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program before retaking a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
The Board may issue a temporary practice certificate to an applicant who:
Has met the appropriate certification requirements to the satisfaction of the Board;
Does not have a criminal record; and
Has not been the subject of a health professional disciplinary action in this State or another jurisdiction.
Unless the Board suspends or revokes a temporary practice certificate, the temporary practice certificate expires 90 calendar days after the date of issuance.
A temporary practice certificate may be extended up to an additional 90 calendar days if the applicant is awaiting the completion of the criminal history records check.
The Board may not issue a certificate to an applicant until the Board has:
Received and reviewed the criminal history record information of the applicant; and
Approved the application.

Unless subject to discipline, the Board shall issue a certificate to each applicant who meets all the requirements of this chapter and Health Occupations Article, §§8-6A-05 and 8-6A-06, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Expiration.
Unless renewed for an additional two-year term, and except as otherwise provided in §A(2) of this regulation, a certificate expires in accordance with the following schedule:
The certificate of a certificate holder with an odd-numbered birth year expires on the 28th day of the certificate holder’s birth month in an odd-numbered year; and
The certificate of a certificate holder with an even-numbered birth year expires on the 28th day of the certificate holder’s birth month in an even-numbered year.
A certificate shall not expire within 180 calendar days of the date of issuance.
Renewal Notice.
At least 3 months before a certificate expires, the Board shall send the certificate holder a renewal notice by either:
First-class mail to the last known address of the certificate holder; or
Electronic means to the last known electronic address of the certificate holder.
The renewal notice shall provide:
The date on which the certificate holder’s certificate is scheduled to expire;

The date by which the Board must receive a renewal application in order for a certificate to remain active until the renewal application submitted by the certificate holder is processed by the Board, in accordance with State Government Article, §10-226(b), Annotated Code of Maryland;
The amount of the renewal fee; and
If the certificate holder is required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §D of this regulation:
Notice that the certificate holder must submit to a CHRC in order to renew the certificate; and
Written instructions for how to complete a CHRC.
It is the responsibility of the certificate holder to:
Be aware of the expiration date of the certificate; and
Renew the certificate before it expires.
Failure of a certificate holder to receive the renewal notice sent by the Board does not relieve the certificate holder of the responsibility to renew a certificate before it expires.
Renewal Requirements.
The Board shall renew a certificate if the individual applying for renewal:
Is otherwise entitled to be certified;
Submits a complete application for renewal on the form required by the Board;
Pays the renewal fee;

Provides satisfactory evidence, as required by the Board, of16 hours of active employment, for compensation, as a nursing assistant within the 2-year period immediately preceding the date of expiration or meet the requirements under §C(2) of this regulation; and
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with § D of this regulation, complies with the requirements of Regulation .04A of this chapter.
If the individual applying for renewal does not have 16 hours of active employment as a nursing assistant within the 2-year period immediately preceding the date of expiration the individual shall:
If a CNA-I, take and pass a nursing assistant competency evaluation; or
If a CNA-II, complete a nursing assistant training program..
Schedule for CHRCs. CHRCs for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the certificate holder’s birth month as follows:
In 2025 — all applicants with an August or September birth month;
In 2026 — all applicants with a September or October birth month;
In 2027 — all applicants with an October or November birth month;
In 2028 — all applicants with a November or December birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a December or January birth month;
In 2030 — all applicants with a January or February birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a February or March birth month;
In 2032 — all applicants with a March or April birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with an April or May birth month;
In 2034 — all applicants with a May or June birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a June or July birth month; and
In 2036 — all applicants with a July or August birth month.
Grace Period. A certificate holder has a 30 calendar day grace period beyond the expiration date of the certificate to renew the certificate.

The Board shall reinstate the certificate of a certificate holder who has failed to renew the certificate for any reason, if the certificate holder meets the renewal requirements in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-08, Annotated Code of Maryland, and Regulation .10 of this chapter.
An applicant for administrative reinstatement who has failed to renew the certificate for a period of 1 year or more shall submit to a CHRC before the certificate is reinstated.
